articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dumped AWS GovCloud keys and internal secrets on GitHub like they're sharing vacation photos. The agency tasked with protecting America's infrastructure just leaked the keys to the kingdom — peak bureaucratic competence.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: Congress finally notices CISA's contractor turned GitHub into their personal classified document dump. Nothing says cybersecurity leadership like accidentally publishing the admin credentials to half the government's cloud infrastructure.

articles.title: 23andMe inherits lawsuit over 'disturbing' DNA data breach
articles.summary: Critical RCE bug in Gogs Git service gets the silent treatment from maintainers for months while exploit modules hit the wild. Open source responsiveness at its finest — crickets with a side of weaponized code.

articles.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
articles.summary: Palo Alto's GlobalProtect gets bypassed harder than airport security circa 2001. CVE-2026-0257 is actively exploited because apparently authentication is more of a suggestion than a requirement.

articles.title: Microsoft threatens legal action against researcher Nightmare Eclipse for exploit disclosure
articles.summary: Microsoft threatens to unleash their 'Digital Crimes Unit' on security researchers for doing their job. Because nothing encourages responsible disclosure like legal intimidation and corporate gaslighting.

articles.title: Microsoft faces security community backlash over Nightmare Eclipse
articles.summary: Microsoft goes full corporate villain mode, threatening researcher Nightmare Eclipse with lawsuits over exploit disclosure. Classic Microsoft: shoot the messenger, ignore the three unpatched zero-days.

articles.title: Dutch cops wrest 17M devices from mystery botnet's clutches
articles.summary: 23andMe inherits a lawsuit over their 2023 DNA data breach where they allegedly paid ransoms and downplayed the mega-leak. Your genetic privacy sold separately, terms and conditions may include criminal exploitation.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: License plate readers evolve from catching criminals to stalking school kids and noise complainers. EFF exposes how surveillance creep turns traffic enforcement into a panopticon with police characteristics.

articles.title: More License Plate Reader Mission Creep: School Residency Verification, Background Checks, and Noise Complaints
articles.summary: Age verification transforms into a privacy apocalypse as lawmakers rush to 'protect' kids by surveilling everyone. EFF warns that checking IDs online means building the surveillance state one birthday at a time.

articles.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-0257) Under Active Exploitation
articles.summary: Dutch authorities dismantle a 17-million-device botnet because apparently the Netherlands doesn't mess around with cyber cleanup. Meanwhile, your smart toaster was probably part of the zombie army.
